text: Because the threat of a change of control leads leaders to take fewer risks in order to avoid triggering conversion, a contingent capital design with increased voting rights allows those leaders to act more in accordance with their moral convictions and conscience.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Reflections on the Possible Application of Contingent Capital in Corporate Governance (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=1998455

isBasedOn.name: Initial Reflections on the Possible Application of Contingent Capital in Corporate Governance

abstract: It could allow SIFI leaders to increasingly act in accordance with their moral convictions and conscience because the threat of change of control may influence SIFI leaders to take fewer risks to avoid triggering the conversion of CCS and a possible change of con- trol.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: where conversion carries a credible threat of change of control
where shareholders respond by allowing management more discretion over risk taking
